subject: Order Form — pricing cadence, invoicing, escrow trigger
messages:
From: Amy Li <amy.li@chronoslabs.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@chronoslabs.com
Date: Sun, 6 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form questions — pricing cadence, invoicing, escrow trigger

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Markus and I reviewed the draft order form (attached) and had a couple of commercial items we need clarified before we can route to procurement:

- Invoicing cadence: does Redwood invoice monthly in arrears or can we do a quarterly invoice in advance? We need to know for cashflow planning.
- Net terms: our AP runs Net45; can Redwood accept Net45 for the first year?
- Minimum commit / proration: the order form language around minimum commit and proration (section 3) is a bit fuzzy — we expect pro-rata credits for partial-quarter usage.
- Tax / VAT: Chronos has EU subsidiaries; please confirm who is responsible for VAT or reverse charge handling.
- Escrow trigger: we request an escrow-style holdback mechanism for the first 90 days (capped at 15% of Q1 spend) to cover data egress and material SLA breaches. We understand this is unusual; we wanted to float it early.

Attached: Chronos_OrderForm_v1.pdf (our annotations). Please advise next steps and whether you need legal to engagement.

Thanks,
Amy Li
Head of Finance, Chronos Labs
amy.li@chronoslabs.com
Attachment: Chronos_OrderForm_v1.pdf (annotated)
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: Amy Li <amy.li@chronoslabs.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 6 Jul 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — pricing cadence, invoicing, escrow trigger

Amy — thanks for the clear list. Quick take from our side and proposed path forward: 

- Invoicing cadence: we typically do monthly in arrears (this gives most customers better matching for usage). We're open to quarterly in advance for larger committed deals — can you confirm which you'd prefer so Ben can model cashflow?
- Net terms: Net45 for year one is plausible; we usually default to Net30 for self-serve but can accommodate Net45 on enterprise order forms with credit check.
- Minimum commit / proration: we agree on pro-rata credits for mid-quarter reductions; Ben, can you propose precise language for section 3 (phasing and proration)?
- Tax / VAT: Kimberly, please confirm VAT reverse-charge handling for EU affiliates and whether we need a VAT residency statement.
- Escrow trigger: this is the biggest policy ask. From a revenue recognition and operational risk standpoint, escrow-like holdbacks create complexity. Attaching a cashflow-waterfall (stub) so the team can see the impact.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben to propose commercial language for minimum commit, proration, and the Q1 escrow cap.
2) Kimberly to confirm tax/VAT ask and whether legal needs to keep escrow language narrow (e.g., specific SLA breach events only).
3) I'll coordinate a short call with Markus / Amy to finalize.

I'll loop Lauren if revenue recognition / accounting needs to weigh in. Are you available for a 30-min call Wednesday (7/9) afternoon PT?

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference
Attachment: cashflow-waterfall.xlsx (stub)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, Amy Li <amy.li@chronoslabs.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jul 2025 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — pricing cadence, invoicing, escrow trigger

Thanks for the context — quick commercial proposal from my side: 

- Invoice cadence: offer two options in the order form: (A) monthly in arrears (default), (B) quarterly in advance with a 2% processing uplift. Let the customer pick at signature.
- Net terms: accept Net45 for year one; include language that Net45 is subject to PO and a one-time credit check (standard).
- Minimum commit phasing: recommend a "staircase" for the first 4 quarters: 40%/60%/80%/100% of committed RUs, with pro-rata credits if usage falls below a tranche. I'll draft exact table for section 3.
- Escrow holdback: alternative to a cash escrow is a capped invoice credit mechanism we can control internally: on material SLA breach (as defined in SLO table) we apply a credit up to the escrow cap on the next invoice or issue a refund. We avoid a third-party escrow to keep revenue recognition simple. If the customer insists on a third-party escrow, limit it to 15% of Q1 spend and a 90-day expiry. 
- VAT: we need the VAT residency statement; if reverse-charge applies for EU affiliates, Chronos must confirm entity-level VAT IDs.

I'll attach a redlined order form (Chronos_OrderForm_v2.pdf) with the staircase table and the proposed credit language for escrow alternative.

Ben Carter
Head of Large Accounts, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Chronos_OrderForm_v2.pdf (commercial redline)
From: Amy Li <amy.li@chronoslabs.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Markus Engel <markus.engel@chronoslabs.com>, procurement@chronoslabs.com
Date: Tue, 8 Jul 2025 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — pricing cadence, invoicing, escrow trigger

Rishi / Ben — thanks, that's headed in the right direction. A few clarifications / counterpoints from Chronos: 

- We prefer quarterly in advance (option B) for cashflow; the 2% uplift is acceptable but we'd like the uplift capped for enterprise customers.
- Net45 ok, but procurement requires the Net45 clause to be explicit and to include PO routing to procurement@chronoslabs.com.
- Stairs: the staircase table looks fine; please ensure proration is automatic (no manual credits).
- Escrow: Chronos insists on a neutral third-party escrow for the first 90 days capped at 15% of Q1 spend. We can accept the invoice-credit fallback only as a secondary remedy. The escrow is meant to cover data egress and catastrophic SLA failure — not minor latency blips.
- VAT: attaching a VAT_residency_statement.pdf for our EU operating entity; please confirm next steps for reverse-charge treatment.

If Redwood is comfortable with a 90-day, capped escrow as primary remedy, we'll greenlight procurement to open the PO. Otherwise we'll need to escalate.

Best,
Amy
Attachment: VAT_residency_statement.pdf
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: Amy Li <amy.li@chronoslabs.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 9 Jul 2025 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — pricing cadence, invoicing, escrow trigger

Amy — appreciate the prompt replies and the VAT file. Quick summary and proposed next steps (so everyone has a single source of truth):

Agreed points: 
- Invoice cadence: we'll present both options in the order form; Chronos will indicate quarterly-in-advance at signature; Ben will limit the uplift to 2% and add a cap for enterprise customers.
- Net terms: Net45 accepted for year one; PO routing to procurement@chronoslabs.com required in the order form.
- Minimum commit & proration: Ben will publish explicit staircase table and automatic proration calculations in section 3 (no manual credits).
- VAT: Kimberly will confirm reverse-charge handling once VAT IDs are validated; thanks for the residency statement, Amy.

Open / legal items: 
- Escrow: Redwood prefers the internal invoice-credit mechanism as primary (faster remediation + simpler accounting). Chronos prefers neutral third-party escrow for the first 90 days capped at 15% Q1 spend.
  - Legal ask: can Redwood legal draft an escrow clause that (a) limits trigger events to material SLA breaches or data egress, (b) caps the amount and duration, and (c) defines release criteria?
  - Accounting ask (Lauren): we need to confirm rev rec treatment if a third-party escrow is used — Lauren, please weigh in on whether the holdback would defer revenue.

Next steps: 
1) Ben to produce the staircase/proration table and update Chronos_OrderForm_v2 with the two invoice cadence options (ETA: 7/10).
2) Kimberly to confirm VAT reverse-charge path after VAT ID validation (ETA: 7/10).
3) Lauren to confirm revenue recognition impact for third-party escrow (ETA: 7/11).
4) Rishi to schedule a 30-min commercial + procurement call for Wed 7/16 10:00 AM PT (proposed) to lock terms. I'll send a calendar invite and a DocuSign link once legal has redlined escrow language.

If that plan works, Amy / Markus please confirm availability for 7/16 10:00 AM PT and we'll proceed. 

Thanks all — forwarding the entire thread below for legal / finance context.
